futility: cmd_update: Add "system property" and '--sys_props' to override When updating firmware, we may need to get some system environment status, like which firmware slot was selected and boot (active), or setting cookies so the next boot will be using right (updated) slot. In verified boot, these status are manipulated by "system property" using API Vb{Get,Set}SystemProperty{String,Int}. The user land tool is `crossystem`. In order to run the firmware updater for testing and debugging, we need an easy way to toggle getting real system status, or fetch from predefined values. A new 'system_property' structure is introduced and included as part of `updater_config`. Each property can be access by `get_system_property(property_type)` function. If the value was not fetched yet, the function will call corresponding 'getter' function defined in property and then cache it. A new parameter '--sys_props` is also introduced so we can easily override them from command line so the updater will not get status from running system. CHROMIUM: net: xfrm: expose xfrm_acq_expires sysctl to namespaces Android P now requires as per CTS that the sysctl /proc/sys/net/core/xfrm_acq_expires be accessible by Android. [autotest] random_mac_address_test_base: filter out low signal Even in our RF shielded cells, some outside traffic may be detected by a packet capture device. Particularly, it appears that our new Gale installations seem a bit more sensitive than Whirlwind. In one sample over ~90 seconds I ~50 packets on channel 1, all in the [-94, -89] dBm range. Longer tests showed similar results. This is sufficiently weak that it shouldn't interfere much with test activity, and it's clearly not traffic from the DUT. Enable low-signal filtering for MAC randomization tests, so we don't bother considering this outside traffic. CHROMIUM: net: xfrm: expose xfrm_acq_expires sysctl to namespaces Android P now requires as per CTS that the sysctl /proc/sys/net/core/xfrm_acq_expires be accessible by Android. More precisely Android P requires to be able to set the value of that sysctl to 1 hour as the Android IpSec api assumes a long timeout value. By default xfrm_ac_expires it set to 30 seconds. The xfrm sysctl handlers defined in net/xfrm/xfrm_sysctl.c are namespace aware so that xfrm_acq_expires can bet set independently for the host and for the Android container, but by default Linux will not make any of the xfrm sysctl available to anything but the init user namespace, which prevents Android running in the ARC container to write its setting. This patch resolves this conflict by exposing xfrm_acq_expires to so that Android running in the ARC container can write to this sysctl.
